description:
Decide how `octo_pi_tui2` consumes Filament Core during and after development. Three options, each with trade-offs.

## Options

**A. Path-dep against `/Users/j5n/Workspace/filament` during development.**
- Pro: instant iteration on upstream API changes; no release cadence.
- Pro: changes in either repo are visible immediately.
- Con: doesn't work for collaborators or CI without local Filament checkout.
- Con: must switch to vendor or hex before any external consumer.

**B. Vendor Filament source into `octo_pi_tui2/deps_vendored/filament/` (or similar).**
- Pro: self-contained; works in CI without external deps.
- Pro: changes pinned to known-good snapshot.
- Con: divergence pressure — Filament evolves, vendored copy goes stale.
- Con: discipline required to sync vendor with upstream.

**C. Filament hex release.**
- Pro: standard Elixir dependency; works everywhere.
- Pro: forces clean release cadence on Filament.
- Con: requires Filament publish discipline; releases gate OctoPi work.
- Con: probably only viable post-flm-3wr stabilization.

## Recommendation

Phase 1 (during flm-3wr active work and opi-tui2-bootstrap): path-dep (A). Iteration speed dominates.

Phase 2 (once flm-3wr ships and OctoPi is in opi-fil-tui or opi-screen): hex release (C). Filament has a stable surface; OctoPi consumes the canonical path.

Phase 3 (any deviation needed): if OctoPi needs Filament changes that haven't shipped upstream, vendor (B) temporarily, with a tracking ticket to upstream the change.

## Acceptance

- Decision documented in this ticket with rationale.
- `mix.exs` configuration matches the chosen strategy.
- README/docs note the dependency setup for new contributors.
- If path-dep: explicit note that this is temporary, with the trigger condition for switching to hex.

## Dependencies

Should land before opi-tui2-bootstrap starts non-trivial work, since the bootstrap epic spins up `apps/octo_pi_tui2` which needs Filament available.
title: Decide Filament dependency strategy: path-dep, vendor, or hex release
